items.title: Notification preferences, collaborative source mode, and more
items.content_html:
Notification preferences

  • Notification preferences: Choose which emails you receive for each event, including comment replies and mentions, thread resolutions, suggestions submitted, accepted, or rejected, automation runs, and product feedback. Configure preferences on the Notifications page of your dashboard.
  • Automation failure emails: Turn on automation run notifications to get an email when a run fails. Mintlify then holds further failure emails until a run succeeds again.
  • Share notifications: Mintlify notifies you when someone shares a page with you.

Editor and collaboration

  • Collaborative source mode: Source mode now supports real-time collaboration. See your teammates' cursors as they work on the same branch as you. Frontmatter edits sync live across visual and source mode. See Real-time editing.
  • Comment reactions: React to a comment with an emoji to acknowledge it without replying. Hover over a reaction to see who reacted, and reacting to someone else's comment notifies its author. See Comments.
  • Selective publish: Select individual changes in the publish menu to publish part of your pending work instead of everything at once.
  • Media on private pages: Upload images and videos to private pages. Private media is served only to people who can open the page, and it is removed when the page is deleted.
  • Editor polish: Search results show page titles and reveal the file in the sidebar, the sidebar lists only Markdown pages by default, the share dialog searches recipients by email address, the emoji suggestion menu has better search relevance, and the agent panel stays available in site settings.

Automations

  • Run scope for manual runs: When you trigger an automation manually, choose whether it reviews changes since a date, the entire site, or a specific pull request. See Run an automation manually.

Analytics

  • Page filter: Filter your analytics to a specific page with the new page dropdown in the dashboard.

API playground

  • Optional field toggles: In the playground modal, required fields sort first and optional fields collapse behind an Expand N optional fields control, with a global toggle in the header. Collapsed fields stay findable. Searching the page for a hidden field name expands the section that contains it, and values you entered persist across collapse and expand.
  • Collapse fields by default: Set expand: false under x-mint: playground on an operation to collapse nested object fields by default. See Collapse playground fields.

Authoring

  • mint test: Generate tests for the code blocks in your docs from the CLI. Runs are saved so you can revisit past reports. See mint test.
  • <MDX> improvements: Headings inside <MDX> blocks merge into the page's table of contents, ## Title {#id} anchors work at any indent, and code blocks inside <MDX> behave like code blocks at the page root. See MDX.
  • Markdown in component titles: Component titles, such as accordion titles, support inline Markdown formatting like code and bold.
  • Table column widths: HTML tables honor the <colgroup> widths you author.

Referrals

  • Enterprise referrals: Enterprise organizations can now participate in the referral program.

Bug fixes

  • Static exports: Static builds bundle your logo files so exported sites no longer reference missing assets.
  • GitLab subgroups: Repositories in nested GitLab subgroups sync correctly.
  • Large repositories: Repositories large enough that GitHub truncates their file listing now sync all files.
  • Assistant citations: Citations that dropped a leading path segment now open the correct page.
  • Authenticated previews: Preview deployments for docs behind authentication serve your changed files.
  • Translations: The translation automation writes locale-prefixed internal links, so newly translated pages link within their own language.
  • OpenAPI cleanup: Deleting an OpenAPI spec removes its generated assets from your site.
  • Custom fonts: Bold text stays bold when you set a custom body font weight.
  • Code feedback: The code snippet feedback popover displays above the table of contents panel.
  • Dismissed banners: Dismissed banners no longer flash on page load.
  • Editor fixes: Reference-style links and Link components render correctly, HTML tables with colspan or classes round-trip without changes, editing a page no longer reformats untouched content, and branch switching no longer causes redirect loops.

items.title: Referral program, custom component styles, and more
items.content_html:
Referral program

  • Refer a team to Mintlify from the Referrals page in your dashboard. When someone you refer starts a Pro plan, both of your organizations receive 50,000 credits. You can earn referral credits for up to three referrals. Available on Pro plans.

Authoring

  • <MDX> component: Wrap content in <MDX> to render Markdown formatting inside JSX expressions, such as conditional content. See MDX.
  • Custom styles on components: Built-in components now accept a className prop, and dynamic Tailwind utilities work inside it.

Editor and collaboration

  • Private page search: Editor search now includes your private pages, and you can open results directly from the search palette. See Private pages.
  • Agent replies to mentions: Mention @mintlify in a comment, suggestion, or reply and the editor agent answers in the same thread, including on private pages. See Ask the Mintlify agent.
  • Clickable agent questions: When the editor agent asks a clarifying question, click an option to answer instead of typing.
  • SVG attachments: Attach SVG files to editor agent messages. See Attach files.
  • Faster branching: Creating a branch in the editor switches you to it instantly and the editor now guides you through branch protection rules.
  • Editor polish: Math expressions update their rendered preview live as you type, the component properties panel has a refreshed design and autosaves your changes, and opening an editor link that belongs to another of your organizations prompts you to switch instead of showing an error.

Automations

  • Redesigned automation runs: The runs tab shows a grouped feed of each run's results, including pull requests, modified pages, and failures, with status filters and a review-needed indicator. See Manage automations.

Analytics

  • mint analytics: View traffic stats, search queries, feedback, and assistant conversations from the CLI. See mint analytics.

Docs and agents

  • Discoverable llms.txt indexes: The root llms.txt now links to the per-section indexes under /_llms, and optional links are indexed by navigation scope. See llms.txt.
  • Index MCP rate limit: The daily rate limit for the Mintlify Index MCP server is raised to 5,000 requests. See Index MCP reference.
  • Publishing permissions for AI apps: Changing whether your MCP server pushes directly to your deploy branch now requires an admin role. Editors see the setting as read-only.

Bug fixes

  • Safari media: Images and videos now load correctly in Safari.
  • Accordions: HTML tables inside accordions render instead of being dropped.
  • Code groups: Expandable code blocks inside a CodeGroup no longer grow past their collapsed height.
  • iOS zoom: Focusing search and assistant inputs on iOS no longer zooms the page.
  • Favicons: Favicon URLs resolve correctly on deployments with a custom base path.
  • API playground: Enum array items render their values instead of type labels.
  • llms.txt languages: Language-specific llms.txt routes are scoped to their language, the default language is prioritized, and llms-full.txt headings and links are normalized.
  • mint format: CLI formatting now matches the editor's output, so formatting a file no longer produces spurious diffs.
  • Editor fixes: Removing a page icon persists, focus returns to the page after toolbar dropdown picks, and deleting the page you have open redirects instead of showing a stale view.
  • Assistant widget: The widget refreshes its configuration before it expires, so long-lived pages keep a working assistant.

items.title: Editor branches, Slack-triggered automations, bulk member invites, and more
items.content_html:
Editor and collaboration

  • Editor branches: When you create a branch, the editor now creates a draft pull request and autosaves changes to Git. You can rename or delete branches, discard autosaved changes, and move pending changes to a new branch. The branch menu is ordered by recent activity, uses per-user branch names, and shows cleaner Draft <date> names for automatically generated branches. See Branching and publishing.
  • Pull requests open as drafts by default: The editor now opens new pull requests in draft state so you can share a preview URL without signaling that the change is ready to merge. Change this on the editor settings page.
  • GitLab merge requests: Merge requests opened in GitLab now sync into editor branches, matching the existing GitHub behavior.
  • Streamlined editor navigation: The editor has a new breadcrumbs row, consolidated page and share controls, sticky sidebar section headers, and a dedicated bottom bar for settings and Ask agent. Site settings open as editor pages instead of a modal. Mobile navigation now uses a simplified top bar and panel-based sidebar for smaller screens.
  • Page access and comments: Request edit access to a private or protected page from the editor and review requests in an approval modal. Comment cards now show profile pictures, and @mentions link to the mentioned user.
  • Duplicate private pages: Duplicate a private page from the editor to start a new draft from existing content.
  • Live preview improvements: Run multiple local previews at once. Navigation changes now propagate to open previews, the agent panel docks on the left, and the preview remains visible during onboarding follow-up turns.

Automations and integrations

  • Slack message trigger: Enterprise customers can run custom automations from new messages in selected Slack channels. The agent evaluates each message and takes action only when warranted. See Trigger an automation from an integration.
  • Redesigned automations page: The automations list has a new layout, and each automation card shows its run count and who created it. See Manage automations.

Docs and delivery

  • Custom SDK reference pages: Use sdk frontmatter to generate documentation for a single SDK symbol while adding your own examples or guidance above it. You can also configure SDK generation for a navigation group. See Customize a page for a single symbol.
  • GraphQL input types: Input type pages are now generated and served on GraphQL API reference sites. See GraphQL setup.
  • nocopy code blocks: Add the nocopy flag to a fenced code block to hide its copy button. For plain-text content such as ASCII diagrams, use a bare nocopy fence. See Hide copy button.
  • Result snippets: Optionally show a one-line content preview beneath each search result, with matching terms highlighted. Enable Result snippets from your dashboard search settings; the setting is off by default. See Result snippets.
  • Scoped llms.txt indexes: Grouped llms.txt indexes are now served per URL segment at /_llms/<segment>.md, so agents can pull one section of your docs instead of the full index.
  • Assistant widget analytics: Analytics events now include the embedding page's current pathname by default and follow client-side navigation. Set analytics.capturePathname to false to opt out. See assistant analytics config.
  • Bulk member invites: Invite up to 250 teammates at once, then review the list and assign a role to each invitee before sending. Pro and Enterprise plans can upload a CSV of email addresses. See Add members to your organization.
  • Universal Search API keys: Universal Search API keys are out of early access. Any organization can now create and manage them from dashboard settings.
  • Analytics in self-hosted deployments: The dashboard analytics tab is now available on self-hosted deployments.

Bug fixes

  • API playground: OpenAPI 3.1 examples and enum values now appear in generated response samples, and Markdown lists in the endpoint modal no longer render double bullets.
  • Search anchors: JSX headings with custom IDs now create the correct search sections and anchors.
  • Inline styles: Inline CSS in a quoted style attribute now renders correctly on your site, in the CLI, and in the editor.
  • Editor components: Copying and pasting inside a Step no longer creates nested steps, tabs no longer jump when clicked, and settings sidebar search has been restored.
  • Editor deep links: Opening an editor link while signed out now returns you to that page after login instead of the dashboard home page.
  • Anchor icons: Anchor link icons remain white when hovering over a dark background.
  • Assistant widget loading: The widget stays interactive while it's loading.
  • Docs MCP: Unknown tool calls now return a JSON-RPC error instead of failing silently, and MCP tool schemas use the 2020-12 JSON Schema dialect.

items.title: June 5, 2026
items.content_html:
Message IDs are Stabilized

The Message ID RFD has moved to Completed and optional Agent-generated messageId fields are stabilized in ACP v1.

Message IDs let clients group streamed chunks into individual messages and detect when a new message begins.

Read the full announcement.

items.title: June 24, 2026
items.content_html:
Model Config Category is Stabilized

The Model Config Option Category RFD has moved to Completed and the model_config category is stabilized.

Agents can classify model-related parameters such as context size or speed and quality trade-offs so clients can present them alongside the main model selector.

Read the full announcement.

items.title: June 25, 2026
items.content_html:
Rust and TypeScript SDKs Reach 1.0

The Rust SDK based on SACP RFD has moved to Completed after both the Rust and TypeScript ACP SDKs reached version 1.0.0.

The releases provide stable foundations for building ACP clients, agents, and protocol adapters in both ecosystems.

Read the full announcement.

items.title: June 29, 2026
items.content_html:
Request Cancellation is Stabilized

The Request Cancellation RFD has moved to Completed and the $/cancel_request notification is stabilized.

Either side can now request cancellation of an outstanding JSON-RPC request by ID without relying on method-specific cancellation.

Read the full announcement.

items.title: July 6, 2026
items.content_html:
Boolean Config Options are Stabilized

The Boolean Config Option Type RFD has moved to Completed and boolean session configuration options are stabilized.

Agents can now expose native on/off controls, while v1 clients explicitly opt in through the session.configOptions.boolean capability.

Read the full announcement.

items.title: LM Studio 0.3.23 — Reasoning content and tool‑calling reliability
items.content_text: For gpt‑oss on POST /v1/chat/completions , reasoning content moves out of message.content and into choices.message.reasoning (non‑streaming) and choices.delta.reasoning (streaming), aligning with o3‑mini ‡ . Tool names are normalized (e.g., snake_case) before being provided to the model to improve tool‑calling reliability ‡ . items.title: LM Studio 0.3.19 — Bug fixes for streaming and tool calls
items.content_text: Corrected usage statistics returned by OpenAI‑compatible streaming responses ‡ . Improved handling of parallel tool calls via the streaming API ‡ . Fixed parsing of correct tool calls for certain Mistral models ‡ .

items.title: LM Studio 0.3.18 — Streaming options and tool‑calling improvements
items.content_text: Added support for the stream_options object on OpenAI‑compatible endpoints. Setting stream_options.include_usage to true returns prompt and completion token usage during streaming ‡ . Errors returned from streaming endpoints now follow the correct format expected by OpenAI clients ‡ . Tool‑calling support added for Mistral v13 tokenizer models, using proper chat templates ‡ . The response_format.type field now accepts "text" in chat‑completion requests ‡ . Fixed bugs where parallel tool calls split across multiple chunks were dropped and where root‑level $defs in tool definitions were stripped ‡ .

items.title: LM Studio 0.3.17 — Tool‑calling reliability and token‑count updates
items.content_text: Token counts now include the system prompt and tool definitions ‡ . This makes usage reporting more accurate for both the UI and the API. Tool‑call argument tokens are streamed as they are generated ‡ , improving responsiveness when using streamed function calls. Various fixes improve MCP and tool‑calling reliability, including correct handling of tools that omit a parameters object and preventing hangs when an MCP server reloads ‡ .

items.title: The 2026-07-28 MCP Specification: A Stateless, Extensible Future
